later_events.mechanism: amendment by strike-and-insert of section 1 (Department/Secretary of Transportation replaced by Homeland Security); clause continues amended

clauses.reason: Section 1 invokes, for the Secretaries concerned and subject to Defense direction, the authority under section 673 of title 10 to order Ready Reserve units and members to active duty (other than for training) for not more than 24 consecutive months, to respond to “the continuing threat posed by Iraq’s invasion of Kuwait”. EO 13286 section 35 (effective March 1, 2003) struck Department of Transportation and Secretary of Transportation references in section 1 and inserted Homeland Security; the clause continued, amended. EO 13350 revoked EO 12743 by name as an order based on the EO 12722 emergency, effective 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 30, 2004. First end: express revocation.

Section 2 invokes the President's authority under 10 U.S.C. 527 to suspend sections 523 to 526 (officer strength and distribution in grade). It rests on the EO 12722 emergency (the preamble is “in furtherance of Executive Order No. 12722, dated August 2, 1990”) and was revoked by name by EO 13350, effective 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 30, 2004. First end: express revocation.

Section 3 invokes the President's authority under 10 U.S.C. 644 to suspend provisions of law on promotion, involuntary retirement or separation of commissioned officers. It rests on the EO 12722 emergency and was revoked by name by EO 13350, effective 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 30, 2004. First end: express revocation.

Section 4 designates and empowers the Secretary of Defense, without further presidential action, to exercise the authority under 10 U.S.C. 527 and 644 invoked by sections 2 and 3. It depends on those sections and the emergency and was revoked with the order by EO 13350, effective 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 30, 2004. First end: express revocation.

Section 5 allows the authorities delegated by sections 1 and 4 to be redelegated to civilian subordinates appointed by the President with Senate consent. It depends on those delegations and was revoked with the order by EO 13350, effective 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 30, 2004. First end: express revocation.

Section 6 states that the order is intended to improve internal management of the executive branch and creates no enforceable right. It is part of the order and ended with it; no held source ended it earlier. EO 13350 revoked the order by name, effective 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 30, 2004. First end: express revocation.

Section 7 makes the order effective immediately and directs its transmission to the Congress and publication. The effectiveness clause lasts as long as the order; no held source dates performance of the transmission directive or shows that anything turned on it, so the clause is treated with the order. EO 13350 revoked the order by name, effective 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 30, 2004. First end: express revocation.

research_rationale:
EO 12743 (signed 1991-01-18; 56 FR 2661) was read in full in the held Federal Register text layer. In furtherance of Executive Order No. 12722 (the national emergency declared on August 2, 1990, over Iraq's invasion of Kuwait), it (sec. 1) invokes the authority of 10 U.S.C. 673 to order Ready Reserve units and members to active duty for up to 24 consecutive months, (secs. 2 and 3) invokes the President's authority under 10 U.S.C. 527 and 644 to suspend officer-strength and promotion, retirement and separation laws, (sec. 4) designates the Secretary of Defense to exercise the sec. 527 and 644 authority, (sec. 5) permits redelegation to Senate-confirmed civilian subordinates, (sec. 6) disclaims private rights and (sec. 7) makes the order effective immediately. Each section is one clause, as the packet's inventory has it. EO 13286 (effective March 1, 2003, by its section 92) section 35 amended section 1 by striking 'the Department of Transportation' and 'the Secretary of Transportation' and inserting Homeland Security equivalents; under the strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) that is an amendment recorded as a later event and the clause continues, amended, until the order ends. EO 13350 (signed 2004-07-29) terminated the national emergency declared in EO 12722 and revoked, by name, “Executive Order 12743 of January 18, 1991”, among orders “that are based on that national emergency”; its section 10 makes it effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 30, 2004. All seven clauses therefore first ended on 2004-07-30 by express revocation, which is also the whole-order end. EO 12743 states no sunset, and the emergency on which it rests continued until EO 13350. No held instrument ended any clause earlier. Working text for EO 13286 is an American Presidency Project transcription (disclosed below); the order's own text and EO 13350 are held Federal Register text layers. Original not an authenticated transcription: the held text is the OCR text layer of the official Federal Register issue; quotations avoid its recognition errors.

savings.reason: EO 13350 states that, under section 202(a) of the National Emergencies Act, termination of the emergency declared in EO 12722 “shall not affect any action taken or proceeding pending but not finally concluded or determined as of the effective date of this order, any action or proceeding based on any act committed prior to such date, or any rights or duties that matured or penalties that were incurred prior to such date”. Call-ups and suspensions made under EO 12743 before July 30, 2004 are therefore saved as acts done, but no part of the order's own commands continued.
